The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{5},$ what is the value of $tan⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/263a4aacc6e2e73b1a7c2f004bd9b3017233fbe768eda56d194d085994b47d58.png)

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $sin⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{24}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $sin⁡\theta $ is negative in the third quadrant. So, $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(-\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5})}{(-\frac{1}{5})}=2\sqrt{6}.
$$
